__comments: Counters are selected as {__name__=~"name(_total)?"}: Grafana Cloud's OTLP ingestion appends _total to prom-client counters, while a direct Prometheus scrape (local dev) keeps the code name. One selector works in both.
Known gap (needs a new metric): per-target success counts for the legacy POST /usage route. Envoy logs that route as path=/usage, and the service logs no per-request success line.
Known gap (needs a new metric): a 404 target-not-found on the modern route has no metric and no log line; it is visible only as an Envoy response_code=404.
Known gap (needs a new metric): per-target ingestor write success. ClickHouse tables are keyed by target, but Grafana has no datasource for Hive's ClickHouse.
Known gap (needs a new metric): rate-limited requests appear only in usage_rate_limit_dropped; the service's 'Rate limited' log line is debug level and absent in production.

panels.description: Reports the usage service finished collecting, per second, by outcome (success, error, not_ready). Errors here happened after authentication; see the Errors row for the cause.
panels.title: Collect outcomes per second

panels.description: Operations buffered in the usage service after a failed Kafka send, waiting for retry. Sustained growth means Kafka is unreachable; it drains to 0 when sends recover.
panels.title: Operations awaiting Kafka retry

panels.description: Operations the usage service gave up on: the fallback queue hit its size limit, or a report could not be split below the Kafka message size limit. Any non-zero value is data loss.
panels.title: Dropped operations per second

panels.description: Ingestor processing errors, and poison pills: messages whose ClickHouse write failed and whose Kafka offset was left uncommitted. The same poison pill repeating means a stuck partition.
panels.title: Ingestor errors per second

panels.description: Operations the ingestor wrote to ClickHouse divided by operations the usage service collected, over the range. Well below 100% for long means a Kafka backlog or ingestor failures; short excursions above 100% are batch timing.
panels.title: Processed %

panels.description: Operations received by the usage service, successfully sent to Kafka (collected), and written to ClickHouse by the ingestor (processed). The three lines should track each other; a persistent gap is loss or lag.
panels.title: Operations per second

panels.description: Reports accepted by the usage service, and the share still arriving in the legacy (v1) format.
panels.title: Reports per second

panels.description: p95 of each stage inside the usage service (report parsing, collect, compress, Kafka send) and of its calls to the commerce service for rate-limit and retention checks.
panels.title: Usage service latency (p95)

panels.description: p95 of the whole HTTP request (receive to respond) and of the handler alone, the async function that runs after the request is parsed. The difference is parsing and auth.
panels.title: HTTP request duration (p95)

panels.description: ClickHouse insert requests per second from the ingestor, by target table and HTTP status. Any series with a non-200 status is rejected inserts.
panels.title: ClickHouse write status

panels.description: Operations, registry records and operation errors the ingestor failed to write to ClickHouse, per second.
panels.title: ClickHouse write failures per second

panels.description: p95 of ingestor message processing (decompress, parse, write) and of each ClickHouse insert by table.
panels.title: Ingestor latency (p95)

panels.description: Reports rejected because the organization is over its usage quota (rate limit answered by the commerce service), by target.
panels.title: Rate-limited reports by target

panels.description: Operations dropped during report validation in the usage service, by reason.
panels.title: Invalid operations by reason

panels.description: Requests rejected before collection: no token, a token without usage:report access, or an unknown legacy token.
panels.title: Auth rejections

panels.description: Requests by x-usage-api-version header value. "invalid" means the client sent no or an unsupported version and was rejected with 401.
panels.title: API version header

panels.description: Non-200 responses on /usage paths from Envoy access logs, by path and status. Filter with the Target ID and Status Code variables.

targets.expr: sum by (path, response_code) (count_over_time({namespace="contour", container_name="envoy"} | json | __error__=`` | path =~ `/usage(/.*)?` | path =~ `/usage(/$targetId.*)?` | response_code =~ `$status` | response_code != 200 [$__interval]))

panels.title: Non-200 responses by target path and status

panels.description: Targets whose reports contained invalid operations, from usage service logs. Use it to find which client to contact.

targets.expr: sum by (target) (count_over_time({container_name="usage-service"} | json | msg =~ `Detected invalid operation.*` | regexp `target=(?P<target>[0-9a-f-]{36})` | target =~ `$targetId` [$__interval]))

panels.title: Invalid operations by target

panels.description: Usage service error log events per interval, by message prefix.

targets.expr: sum by (event) (count_over_time({container_name="usage-service"} | json | msg =~ `(Report validation failed|Detected invalid operation|Failed to collect|No access|Token not found|Failed to check rate limit|Failed to get retention info|Not ready to collect report).*` | regexp `"msg":"(?P<event>[A-Za-z][A-Za-z ]*[A-Za-z])` [$__interval]))

panels.title: Usage service error events

panels.description: Raw usage service error log lines behind the events above, filtered by Target ID.

targets.expr: {container_name="usage-service"} | json | msg =~ `(Report validation failed|Detected invalid operation|Failed to collect|No access|Token not found|Failed to check rate limit|Failed to get retention info|Not ready to collect report).*` | targetId =~ `$targetId` or target =~ `$targetId`

panels.title: Usage service error details

panels.description: Ingestor log lines for messages whose write failed and were left uncommitted, so the affected target id can be read from the message.
panels.title: Poison-pill messages (targets affected)

panels.description: Requests on /usage paths from Envoy access logs, grouped by path (the target id). The legacy route has no target in the path and shows as /usage.

targets.expr: sum by (path) (count_over_time({namespace="contour", container_name="envoy"} | json | __error__=`` | path =~ `/usage(/.*)?` | path =~ `/usage(/$targetId.*)?` [$__interval]))

panels.title: Requests by target path (legacy route shows as /usage)

panels.description: Node.js event loop lag per pod. A sustained p99 above ~100 ms means the process is CPU-bound and cannot keep up with HTTP / Kafka / ClickHouse I/O.

panels.title: usage-ingestor-service · event loop lag (p50 / p99)

panels.description: Seconds spent in V8 garbage collection per second, per pod (all GC kinds). Values approaching 0.1 (10%) indicate heap pressure; correlate with the memory panel above.

targets.expr: sum by (event) (count_over_time({container_name="usage-service"} | json | msg =~ `Kafka producer: (disconnected|request timeout)` | regexp `Kafka producer: (?P<event>[a-z ]+)` [$__interval]))
